input.quote: Nothing herein is intended nor shall be construed as creating an exclusive arrangement between Customer and Kubient. This Agreement will not restrict Customer offering Inventory via other agents or otherwise selling Inventory to any third parties.
input.rationale: The agreement contains no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay obligation, shortfall penalty or volume cap on us. Economics are a pure revenue share on actual activity: under § 5 (p0023) "The Parties agree to share any revenue generated as a result of this Agreement, or Customer's use of the Services," with Kubient paying us within seven days of its own receipt — we owe no committed spend. § 1 (p0001) expressly disclaims exclusivity and confirms the agreement "will not restrict Customer offering Inventory via other agents or otherwise selling Inventory to any third parties," so there is no volume restriction on us either. § 13 (p0062) only disclaims any guaranteed "minimum level of revenue or profit," which is a vendor-side disclaimer rather than a commitment by us. This meets the preferred position (no minimum commitment; fees tied to actual usage), so no redline is warranted. Noted for context only, and not flagged under this rule: § 4(a) (p0016) bars termination for convenience during the one-year Initial Term and lets Kubient keep fees generated during the termination period — but since those are fees actually generated rather than a committed minimum, it creates no take-or-pay exposure; any concern with the term/termination mechanics belongs to the termination rule.
